labelingRule: COLLIDE = an agent choosing between these two from descriptions alone would be genuinely unsure (same job, different words). DISTINCT = the choice is obvious, INCLUDING when the two are lexically similar but explicitly disjoint in scope.
notes: A label is a judgement, not a measurement. If you disagree with one, change it deliberately and let the metrics move - that is the corpus working as intended. What you must not do is retune a label to make a scorer pass. Pairs marked provenance "verbatim shipped descriptions" use real frontmatter and must not be edited; synthetic pairs exist to isolate one discrimination each and may be extended.

classes.paraphrase-low-overlap: COLLIDE with little shared surface text - the class surface metrics miss.
classes.overlapping-scope: COLLIDE where both descriptions plainly claim the same request.
classes.mutual-exclusion-high-overlap: DISTINCT despite heavy shared vocabulary, disjoint by explicit boundary.
classes.same-artifact-opposite-capability: DISTINCT: same artifact, read vs write.
classes.house-template: DISTINCT: unrelated skills sharing boilerplate prose - the template trap.
classes.unrelated: DISTINCT: no meaningful relation, the easy negatives.
classes.non-latin: Script the text metrics cannot read; expected to be flagged low text coverage.

a.name: pdf
a.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.

b.name: pdf-reading
b.description: Use this skill when you need to read, inspect, or extract content from PDF files — especially when file content is NOT in your context and you need to read it from disk. Covers content inventory, text extraction, page rasterization for visual inspection, embedded image/attachment/table/form-field extraction, and choosing the right reading strategy for different document types (text-heavy, scanned, slide-decks, forms, data-heavy). Do NOT use this skill for PDF creation, form filling, merging, splitting, watermarking, or encryption — use the pdf skill instead.

pairs.notes: Both claim reading and extracting from PDFs; for "read this PDF" the choice is genuinely unsure.
